blocks.alt: Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 1, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- **Parallel **lines are equidistant meaning they never meet
- **Parallel** lines have **equal** **gradients**

blocks.alt: Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 2, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes
Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 3, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- **Perpendicular** lines meet at **right** **angles**
- The **product** of their **gradients** is -1

blocks.alt: Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 4, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md:
- **Collinear** line segments are two line segments that are part of the **same** line
- They have **equal** **gradients**

  - They may **pass** through, or **meet** at, a common **point**
  - When they are extended, they become the same line
- **Rearrange** their equations into the same form and they will be identical

blocks.alt: Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 5, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.text: How do I tell if lines are parallel or perpendicular?

blocks.md:
- Rearrange equations into the form **y = mx + c**
- **m** is the **gradient**

blocks.alt: Parallel & Perpendicular Gradients Notes Diagram 6, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Exam questions are good at “hiding” parallel and perpendicular lines.
- For example a **tangent** and a **radius** are **perpendicular.**
- **Parallel lines** could be implied by phrases like “… at the same rate …”
